scenarios.help: One row per conversation: opening_message, persona_goal, facts, account_seed (the customer's account, merged into the starting data), expected_actions and forbidden_actions (tool calls), reply_rubric. Each row becomes a task with a simulated customer, graded by its own checks: no code to write.
scenarios.placeholder: {"opening_message": "I was charged twice for order B-3001", "persona_goal": "Get the duplicate charge refunded", "expected_actions": [{"tool": "issue_refund", "args": {"order_id": "B-3001"}}], "forbidden_actions": ["apply_credit"]}
scenarios.shapeAuto: first task with a simulated customer
scenarios.switchGrader: Grade this benchmark by its checks
scenarios.switchGraderHint: Needed when the benchmark grades another way. Its other tasks keep their own checks and need their readiness checks again.
scenarios.previewSummary: {{ok}} rows become tasks, {{bad}} rows have problems.
scenarios.graderChanged: The benchmark is now graded by its checks.

mock.help: Upload your API's OpenAPI file to get a stand-in service: the same routes over HTTP and one tool per operation, over starting data each task seeds, with the final data exported for the checks. Calls recorded in a run can be added as fixed answers with heimdall mock fixtures.
mock.idHint: Lowercase letters, digits, - or _; tasks name the service by it.
mock.replace: Replace the service if it exists (drops its recorded answers)
mock.serviceYaml: Add this to each task that uses the service (task.yaml, under services:)
mock.seed: And its starting data, in the task's seed file
